title: Durable Claude launcher authority ports
description: Objective: make the landed @moe/runner Claude launcher composable with daemon-durable one-use grant consumption and launch registration without replacing its production runtime-pin, Job Object, lock, duplicate, and process-observation defaults. Deliverable: a narrow public launcher factory/port overlay that retains all production defaults except caller-supplied consumeGrant/registerLock authority ports, invokes those ports at the existing pre-open/post-start linearization points, and accepts only exact durable CAS/registration outcomes. Consumer: task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9. NOT in scope: daemon persistence, schema, claim/activation construction, HTTP ingress, provider policy, or changing the default launchClaude behavior. Current measured gap at HEAD 284d5dd: launchClaude accepts only an all-or-nothing ClaudeLauncherDependencies override; its defaults and constituent production ports are not public, while pre-consuming a grant causes GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED and leaving the pure default cannot durably close a crash between open and observation.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/runner factory or overlay creates a Claude launcher that uses the shipped runtime pin, duplicate resolver, Windows Job boundary, OS lock, observation, clock and delay defaults while replacing only grant-consumption and launch-registration ports.

The injected grant port performs an exact one-use CAS at the existing pre-open grant phase; a committed UNUSED grant can advance once, replay/forgery/wrapper drift pins the exact delegated code and layer, and no physical open occurs on refusal or thrown/malformed fulfillment.

The injected registration port records the pending and observed process identities at the existing launcher phases; duplicate/restart delivery adopts or refuses from the durable registration before a second physical open.

All injected outcomes remain total under the landed descriptor/native-Promise containment and cleanup precedence; generated hostile cases assert positive cardinality, exact code/layer, open count, close/release order, and no secret echo.

@moe/runner root exports the factory/overlay and complete type closure; bare-root Node smoke uses real defaults with no deep import, focused runner typecheck/tests pass, and task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 is recorded as the production consumer.
taskRails: Preserve launchClaude default behavior for existing callers; do not export individual internal default ports or permit a caller to replace the Windows physical boundary piecemeal.
Use TDD; every refusal pins exact stable code and layer, and mutation drills prove the injected consume/register calls precede physical open/relaunch.
Use only public package roots across consumers; exact LF runtime bridges; target <=250 physical lines and split before 400.
No daemon/store code or test-owned authority in this runner task.

DESIGN CHOICE THAT MAKES THE DELEGATION ASSERTIONS NON-VACUOUS: the two stubs are DURABLE STORES that answer from their OWN rows, never from the caller's bytes. `durableGrants` seeds a row, looks it up by the presented grantId, and runs the production `consumeActivationGrant` over the STORED record, CASing the row on success. So:
- replay = stored row is CONSUMED while the caller presents its committed UNUSED grant -> GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED/GRANT. The default port, handed the same request, would SUCCEED. D1 must redden this.
- wrapper drift = stored row is bound to `wrapper-other` while the presented grant and wrapperIdentity agree with each other -> GRANT_WRAPPER_MISMATCH/GRANT. Default would also succeed here, so this case is D1-sensitive too (a grant tampered to disagree with itself is unusable: `validateActivationCommit` re-derives the grantId from `initialGrantBinding(intentId, grant.wrapperIdentity)` and would refuse ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT upstream, so the drift has to live in the durable row).
- forgery = grantId absent from the store -> ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT/ACTIVATION, a code+layer pair the default consumeGrant CANNOT emit at the grant phase (it only ever emits EFFECT_GRANT_MALFORMED/KERNEL, GRANT_WRAPPER_MISMATCH/GRANT, GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED/GRANT). That makes delegation provable from the code alone.

PLAN DEVIATION, one item, deliberate. Step 2 case (7) lists "prototype-only property" among the shapes that must refuse CLAUDE_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY_UNUSABLE. That is factually wrong against the port the plan itself mandates: step 5 requires binding with the exported `readCapability`, which walks up to PROTOTYPE_DEPTH=4 prototypes precisely so a CLASS INSTANCE binds (its own comment says a plain-record reader "would refuse production"). A daemon adapter class is the expected production shape. I therefore inverted that one case into a POSITIVE control — "accepts an authority whose ports live on a class prototype", asserting OBSERVED plus both phases, with the stub using `this` so the `Reflect.apply(candidate, source, args)` receiver is also pinned. The other six unusable shapes (null, primitive, proxy, absent consume, absent commit, non-function, getter-backed) are swept and counted.

COVERAGE MAP to the plan's nine clauses: (1) happy path — exactly one consume call with `[COMMIT.grant, CLAIM.wrapperIdentity]`, row advances to CONSUMED/version+1, OBSERVED/PROVEN, trace pins ["runtime","validate","lock","open","observe","unlock"] (no "consume"/"register" because the overlay replaces those two fixture ports). (2)(3) replay/forgery/drift as above, each asserting trace === ["runtime","validate"] so zero lock and zero open. (4) exactly 2 commits, phases ["PREFLIGHT","STARTED"], processIdentities ["pending:wrapper-1","windows:4242:134309515541692727"], `claim` identity-equal to CLAIM, `prior` null, and commit:PREFLIGHT strictly before "open" in one shared trace. (5) priorRegistration reusing DIGEST -> LAUNCH_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_REUSED/LAUNCH_LOCK with regs.commits.length === 0 and grants.calls.length === 1, proving the PURE layer answered and the injected port was never reached. (6) duplicateDelivery with NO deps at all — real shipped defaults — asserting EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH and ADOPTED with zero authority calls; this is D4's target. (7) 7 unusable shapes, all CLAUDE_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY_UNUSABLE/LAUNCHER with trace === []. (8) generated matrix = 8 grant fulfilments + 7 registration fulfilments x 2 phases = 22, hand-written count pinned by `expect(MATRIX.length).toBe(22)` plus a unique-name check and two partition counts (8 GRANT, 7 with opens===1) so a silently shrunk generator cannot pass; each case pins exact code+layer, exact open count, and for the STARTED family that "close" precedes "unlock". (9) `expectNoSecretEcho` on every refusal: no bootstrap digest, no grantId, no pinned executable path.

implementationPlan.description: Implement claude-launcher-authority.ts until step 2's suite is green. `createClaudeLauncher(authority: unknown)` returns `(value: unknown, options?: ClaudeLaunchOptions) => Promise<ClaudeLaunchResult>`. At CONSTRUCTION, bind both authority capabilities exactly once with the exported `readCapability` from claude-launcher-port-results.js (never reimplement descriptor/proxy safety); if either is null, return a launcher that refuses CLAUDE_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY_UNUSABLE at LAUNCHER without touching any port. Otherwise the returned launcher calls `launchClaude(value, {...options, deps: overlay})` where overlay = `{...(options?.deps ?? CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_DEFAULTS), consumeGrant, registerLock}` — the authority slots ALWAYS win, and the eight other slots are the shipped defaults whenever the caller supplies no deps. `consumeGrant(grant, wrapperIdentity)` delegates STRAIGHT to `consumeGrantDurably` — it must NOT pre-run the pure `consumeActivationGrant`, or replay would be answered by the pure layer and the delegated-code assertion would go vacuous. `registerLock(registration, claim, prior)` calls the PURE `registerLaunchLock` first and returns its outcome verbatim unless it is REGISTERED; on REGISTERED it classifies the phase from the validated registration's processIdentity using the step-3 constants (exact `pendingProcessIdentity(registration.wrapperIdentity)` match -> PREFLIGHT, the started prefix -> STARTED, anything else -> a LAUNCH_LOCK_MALFORMED refusal at LAUNCH_LOCK) and returns `commitProcessRegistration({phase, registration, claim, prior})` raw for the launcher's existing `decodeRegistration` to validate. Both wrappers stay SYNCHRONOUS and add NO try/catch — the launcher's `contained()` and lifecycle's try/catch own containment and layer attribution. A module doc comment names the production consumer task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9. Keep the file under 250 physical lines.

THREE DECISIONS THAT DEPART FROM THE STEP TEXT, all measured, none narrowing.

1. OPTIONS ARE READ WITH `snapshotLaunchEntry`, NOT SPREAD. Step 5 specified `launchClaude(value, {...options, deps: overlay})`. A spread of a caller-supplied Proxy runs an ownKeys trap in OUR frame, outside every containment, and the returned promise would REJECT instead of refusing — the launcher's whole contract is that it never rejects. So the overlay reads the options with the launcher's own strict reader and, when that reader refuses (hostile options, or caller deps that fail `snapshotLauncherPorts`), forwards the ORIGINAL options so `launchClaude` computes the same refusal itself. Behaviour for every well-formed caller is identical; the difference is only that a hostile one now gets a refusal instead of a rejection. Likewise the base port set is the FROZEN result of `snapshotLauncherPorts` rather than a raw spread of `entry.deps`, so a hostile deps object is never spread either.

2. `durableRegistrationPort(commit)` IS FACTORED OUT AND EXPORTED (module-level, NOT on the seam). Reason: the classifier's third arm — "identity matches neither declared format" -> LAUNCH_LOCK_MALFORMED/LAUNCH_LOCK — is UNREACHABLE through `launchClaude` today, because both call sites now build their identity with the step-3 builders, so `registerLaunchLock` can only ever hand back `pending:<wrapper>` or `windows:<pid>:<time>`. I traced this rather than assuming it. An unreachable guard asserted by nothing is exactly the "guard detached from its subject" failure the epic rail warns about, so the port is exported and pinned DIRECTLY on the production function: one test drives a `linux:4242:1` identity through it and asserts the exact code, the exact layer, AND that the durable commit was never called; a second drives a claim-binding conflict and asserts the PURE refusal comes back verbatim with the commit still uncalled. This is a production surface, not a test helper reimplementing one.

3. `classifyRegistrationPhase` is also exported and swept over all four identity shapes (pending-for-this-wrapper -> PREFLIGHT, started -> STARTED, pending-for-ANOTHER-wrapper -> null, foreign prefix -> null). The third case matters: the PREFLIGHT arm is an EXACT `pendingProcessIdentity(registration.wrapperIdentity)` match, not a `pending:` prefix test, so a pending identity naming a different wrapper is refused rather than silently accepted.

ADDENDUM 2 (comment-c1496f52, port shape) — ADOPTED IN FULL. 1) ADD A NEW PORT KEY (e.g. `commitRegistration`) to PORT_KEYS — REJECTED. `snapshotLauncherPorts` requires every PORT_KEYS entry, so every existing caller and test that hands a full `deps` object (index-surface.test.ts:499, the fixture's `dependencies()`) would start returning null and the launcher would refuse. port-results.ts is also already at exactly 250 lines. 2) LET THE INJECTED PORT REPLACE `registerLaunchLock` OUTRIGHT — REJECTED, and this is the correction in comment-c1496f524e6241a1aaa327557f2c30d6. The daemon would have to reimplement claim binding, one-time-credential reuse and prior-conflict authority. The overlay COMPOSES instead: pure `registerLaunchLock` runs first at both phases, and only its REGISTERED outcome is handed to the injected port.

3) PRE-RUN pure `consumeActivationGrant` BEFORE the injected CAS — REJECTED. It would answer replay with GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED from the PURE layer, so the durable-replay test would be answered by an earlier guard and would stay green even if the injected CAS were deleted. It fabricates a process identity and, once read back as `priorRegistration` on a restart, makes `registerLaunchLock` refuse LAUNCH_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_REUSED instead of adopting. The launcher therefore hands the port an explicit PREFLIGHT/STARTED phase and never decides what the daemon persists; the daemon may reserve at PREFLIGHT and commit only at STARTED. This is how DoD 3's 'records the pending and observed process identities at the existing launcher phases' is satisfied without inventing authority.
